name: Malolotja Nature Reserve
subtitle: Malolotja is an 18,000 ha reserve in north-west Eswatini, managed by the National Trust Commission since 1979.

facts.label: Area
facts.value: Over 18,000 ha, the largest proclaimed protected area in Eswatini

facts.label: Management
facts.value: Managed by the Eswatini National Trust Commission since 1979

facts.label: Habitats
facts.value: Wetland, woodland, highveld grassland and mistbelt forest

facts.label: Birds
facts.value: More than 280 bird species recorded, over half Eswatini's total

facts.label: Ngwenya Mine
facts.value: Modern open-cast mining ran from 1958 until 1979; people mined the iron ore over 43,000 years ago

facts.label: Mining licence
facts.value: In February 2024 Michael Lee Enterprises was granted a 25-year mining licence

facts.label: Mining pressure
facts.value: The company plans to mine an additional 400 ha, with irreversible damage to Mgwayiza Valley, according to GroundUp

facts.label: Authorisation
facts.value: No environmental authorisation had been given as of June 2024

parts.text: Malolotja is an 18,000 ha reserve in north-west Eswatini, managed by the National Trust Commission since 1979. It protects grassland, wetland and forest habitats and more than 280 bird species. In 2024 reporters documented green chert mining inside it, which the company was licensed to expand.
